explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - LEANN is a full‐stack, open-source vector database and RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) toolkit written in Python with C++/CMake backends.  
   - Purpose: Provide a lightweight, on-device vector index (HNSW, DiskANN) that stores only a pruned graph and recomputes embeddings on-demand, enabling semantic search and chat over personal data (files, emails, browser history, code, WeChat, etc.) with minimal storage.  

2. Analyze the file structure  
   Top-level directories:  
   • apps/ – Sample RAG applications (document_rag, email_rag, browser_rag, wechat_rag, code_rag)  
   • packages/  
     – leann-core/ Core Python library: API (Builder, Searcher, Chat), CLI entry point, registry, metadata filter  
     – leann-backend-hnsw/ HNSW graph backend (C++ code, embedding server, CSR conversion)  
     – leann-backend-diskann/ DiskANN backend (third-party DiskANN integration, embedding server)  
     – leann-mcp/ MCP glue for Claude Code integration  
     – wechat-exporter/ Helper for exporting WeChat histories  
   • scripts/ CI & release scripts  
   • benchmarks/ Performance & storage comparison scripts  
   • docs/ Guides, architecture overview, configuration  
   • tests/ Unit & integration tests  
   Other: README.md, pyproject.toml, .github/workflows for CI.  

3. Examine the README for additional insights  
   - Architecture section describes:  
     • Graph-based selective recomputation  
     • High-degree preserving pruning  
     • Two-level search, dynamic batching  
   - Technology stack: Python 3.9–3.13, ZeroMQ/Protobuf servers, optional MKL/OpenBLAS, uv CLI, LLM providers (OpenAI, Ollama, HuggingFace).  

4. Designing the system diagram  
   a. Main components  
     1. Frontend/CLI & Sample Apps  
        • CLI (`leann` command)  
        • apps/*.py scripts for different data sources  
     2. Core Library (leann-core)  
        • LeannBuilder, LeannSearcher, LeannChat  
        • Registry & plugin loader for backends  
        • Metadata filter, interface definitions  
     3. Backends (HNSW, DiskANN)  
        • Embedding servers (ZeroMQ gRPC, Protobuf)  
        • Graph storage (CSR files, pruned graph)  
        • Search algorithms (two-level traversal)  
     4. Storage  
        • Index files (.leann/indexes/…)  
        • Pruned graph + metadata JSON  
     5. External Services  
        • Embedding providers (OpenAI API, Ollama, HuggingFace)  
        • LLM for chat (same providers)  
        • Data exporters (Apple Mail, Chrome profile, WeChatTweak)  
   b. Relationships & data flows  
     • CLI / apps invoke Core API →  
     • Core API calls Builder/Searcher →  
     • Builder loads data (documents, emails, browser history, etc.) → chunking & metadata →  
       • Calls embedding server or remote embedding provider →  
       • Builds pruned graph → writes index files  
     • Searcher: loads graph → on query, traverses graph → fetches missing embeddings via recomputation →  
       • Returns nearest neighbors → Chat wraps results + sends to LLM provider → returns response  
   c. Architectural patterns & principles  
     • Plugin architecture for backends (searcher_base, registry)  
     • Separation of concerns:  
       – Data ingestion (apps)  
       – Index building & searching (core)  
       – Storage (files)  
       – Compute (local embedding server vs external API)  
     • Resource efficiency: graph recomputation, CSR storage  
   d. Key technologies & libraries  
     • Python packages: leann-core, click (CLI), ZeroMQ, Protobuf  
     • C++/CMake backends: DiskANN, HNSW implementations  
     • LLM/embedding: OpenAI, HuggingFace, Ollama  
     • Build tooling: uv, pyproject.toml  

5. Tailoring the diagram for this full-stack vector DB  
   - Draw clear boundary between:  
     • User-facing layer (CLI & apps)  
     • Library core layer (Builder/Searcher/Chat)  
     • Backend compute layer (HNSW/DiskANN embedding servers)  
     • Storage layer (index & metadata files)  
     • External services (LLM & embedding providers, data exporters)  
   - Emphasize data flows: ingest → embed → build graph → query → recompute → chat  

6. Diagram guidelines  
   - Use distinct shapes/colors:  
     • Frontend/apps – rectangles in blue  
     • Core library – rounded rectangle in green  
     • Backends – cylinders or modules in orange  
     • Storage (files) – cylinder icons in grey  
     • External services – cloud shapes in purple  
   - Label each component clearly  
   - Draw directional arrows showing:  
     • Build path (Data Source → Builder → Embedding Server → Graph Storage)  
     • Query path (Query → Searcher → Graph + Recompute → Results → Chat → LLM)  
   - Annotate arrows with protocols or formats (e.g., ZeroMQ/gRPC, JSON index files)  

7. Capture essential details  
   - Include: plugin registry, metadata filtering, AST chunking component in code_rag  
   - Show optional paths (HNSW vs DiskANN) side by side  
   - Indicate how MCP integration plugs into Claude Code via `leann-mcp`  

By following these steps and layering components from user-facing scripts down to low-level graph backends, you’ll create a comprehensive, accurate system design diagram tailored to LEANN’s architecture.
